quotes.text: The arrangements were almost always gorgeous and always very different from what others were doing and the lyrics were always profound, bombastic (if you prefer, 'overblown') and memorable.
Everyone in the band (they all contributed songs) was willing and able to be honest to the world and bear their heart and soul in the music.

This was not a normal rock band, and if you're in the market for 'kick ass rock and roll tunes,' look elsewhere. It's not that Hayward was at all bad on his guitars or Lodge on his bass, and Edge was very solid on drums. It's just these were not the primary catalysts of the group's sound.
Ray Thomas was one of a VERY select few to make extensive use of the flute in pop music. He used it for pure melodic beauty and to add to the grandeur of the tunes.

The mellotron of Mike Pinder was even more predominant in the sound. The very fact that he had such skill in controlling and taming the mellotron in and of itself qualifies him as one of the great underrated keyboardists of all time.

The Moody Blues were a unique group even before a member of the US ping pong team brought one of their albums into China. More than any other successful group, including the early Beatles, they are leaderless. All five members are poets and composers who contribute equally to the production of about one album of original material every ten months.

More than any Moodies album to date, EBGDF highlights the individual songwriting abilities of the five "poets and composers." The group's decision to forgo another attempt at creating a concept album gave each member the freedom to write about what was important to them without having to worry about linking the compositions to an overall theme.

the collaborative spirit of the album is obvious in the significant contributions made by all of the members on each other's songs. In the end, Every Good Boy Deserves Favour achieves the goal of nearly every form of art: the perfect balance between unity and variation.
The Moodies embraced JFK's idealism and truly believed that the exploration of space represented a large step in the evolution of the human race.
The Moodies wanted to open the album with a simulation of a Saturn V rocket blasting off into space, so they contacted NASA and asked them to share any liftoff tapes they had lying around.

The Moodies contacted NASA for a real rocket liftoff recording, but when they listened to the tape, it sounded like a damp squib, so they had to set about creating their own rocket sound, which ended up sounding more authentic.
